rulings.challenge_claim: LF: device_notes mislabels the MT 5:8 adjuration variant's opening particle, splicing the two attested clauses' particles into a form that matches neither. OL: 'the mah-timtze'u shape' is not attested anywhere - MT 5:8 reads the conditional particle with that verb and its interrogative attaches to a different verb, so the attested contrast is the im-timtze'u / mah-tagidu shape.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENT - the two primaries name the SAME defect, reached independently, and it is upheld on bytes. oshb:Song.5.8 opens הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם and then carries TWO distinct clauses, אִֽם תִּמְצְאוּ֙ (conditional particle plus its verb) and מַה תַּגִּ֣ידוּ (interrogative particle plus a different verb), byte tier. device_notes calls this 'the mah-timtze'u shape', grafting the interrogative of the second clause onto the verb of the first - a name matching neither attested clause, and written in the very note that claims formula-variation discipline. The remainder of the row's oath objects re-verify independently rather than by reproduction: oshb:Song.8.4 carries מַה תָּעִ֧ירוּ וּֽמַה תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ and no gazelle-and-doe pairing, against בִּצְבָא֔וֹת א֖וֹ בְּאַיְל֣וֹת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה plus אִם תָּעִ֧ירוּ וְֽאִם תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ in the fuller form; בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם is the daughters vocative rather than the from-phrase; MT 8:4 is genuinely the fourth of exactly four oath sites and הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ at oshb:Song.5.9 is correctly excluded as the daughters quoting the oath back, and is correctly mirrored in the refs; the setumah is in the inventory at MT 8:4 under the claimed type, MT-keyed, disclosed single-witness; the curly WEB span at web:Song.8.4 passes an exact-substring test against the staged verse text (it is the whole verse); and MT 8:4 sits outside the offset zone, so the bare web: refs are legitimate there and no dual is owed. NEW FINDING (neither primary): the formula-variation note discloses only the missing gazelle-and-doe pairing, but MT 8:4 also differs from the fuller form in SPELLING - תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ at oshb:Song.8.4 is defective where the fuller form reads plene, תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ at oshb:Song.2.7 and תְּעֽוֹרְר֛וּ at oshb:Song.3.5 - an undisclosed mater-lectionis pair standing inside the row's own variation claim, in a book where sweeping per attested spelling is a standing hazard rule and where the note's whole point is which elements of the formula vary. Established at byte tier and not previously on the record: oshb:Song.2.7 and oshb:Song.3.5 are byte-identical to one another across the full pointed text, accents included, so both primaries' tier-unlabelled 'MT 2:7 = MT 3:5' holds at the strictest tier. Audited and deliberately NOT raised: MT 8:4 is also paseq-bearing (inventory, single-witness, count-only) while the row discloses only the setumah - the mark arm's paseq rule is a position-claim WARN and not a disclosure duty, and it returns GREEN on this row, so no symmetry defect arises. Severity: LF graded this low and OL medium; medium is right. It is a byte-false Hebrew form label in row prose - the class carried at high severity where the false form is the row's own span token driving an address-direction argument - but here it labels a comparison verse outside the span and no boundary warrant rests on it.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the invented shape name with the attested contrast - the conditional clause plus its separate interrogative clause at oshb:Song.5.8, both openings spliced at byte tier - and disclose the plene/defective pair alongside the missing gazelle-and-doe pairing so the variation claim covers every element that actually varies. Test the cure must pass: every formula SHAPE NAME in the note must be re-spliced from the verse it names and re-collated at byte tier before the row ships - the check 'mah-timtze'u' fails, since no such sequence exists in the book at any tier - and the plene/defective disclosure must name the attested spelling on each side rather than a harmonised form.

rulings.challenge_claim: MT 5:8 is the verse whose shape is being contrasted and it appears in no evidence ref while its neighbour 5:9 does; and 'held earlier in this part' is a positional/part reference in row prose, where cross-row references are supposed to be verse-anchored.
rulings.grounds: Upheld, and OL's two defects are ONE defect with two faces rather than two independent ones. boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Song.8.4, oshb:Song.8.4, web:Song.2.7, web:Song.3.5, web:Song.5.9 and web:Song.8.1-Song.8.3: the contrasted verse web:Song.5.8 = oshb:Song.5.8 is absent while its immediate neighbour 5:9 is present, and the register breach is the mechanism - the contrast is carried by the unanchored positional phrase 'held earlier in this part', which names no verse and additionally imports writer-part and file-order talk into row prose. Because no verse is named, the ref-mirror arm returns GREEN: that rule binds verses argued in prose, and an unanchored reference argues one without naming it. This is the same evasion class recorded as a new finding on P02-015 and P02-013 in the first attempt, making P02-016 its third instance in this cluster - a class, not a spot. The row's own practice one clause later proves the cure is available and cheap: the quoted-back oath at 5:9 is verse-anchored, argued, and mirrored. NEW FINDING (neither primary): the isolation warrant itself is stated as conformity to a governance rule - 'held as its own row per the hybrid rule's isolated bracket treatment' in boundary_rationale, repeated as 'the hybrid rule isolates it as its own bracket unit' in strongest_rejected_alternative - where the governing text requires bracket function to be ARGUED FROM BYTES with the parashah shadow kept as corroboration only. Two faults in one: governance-rule narration in row prose, and a warrant that cites a rule where evidence is owed. The BOUNDARY itself survives on the row's own bytes, so this is a prose and warrant repair and not a boundary challenge: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי opening oshb:Song.8.4 is an attested formula anchor and therefore tier-1 under the moderate voice-attribution policy, so a qualifying marker does sit at this row's front seam - which is also why the neighbouring row's decision to stop before 8:4 was upheld rather than challenged in the first attempt.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace 'held earlier in this part' with the verse-anchored form naming web:Song.5.8 = oshb:Song.5.8, and mirror that ref into boundary_evidence_refs; boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the governance-rule narration and argue the bracket function from the row's own bytes - the attested oath formula opening the verse, its daughters vocative, and the shape it does NOT carry - keeping the setumah as corroboration only, single-witness. Run the anchoring as a SWEEP across the part together with P02-013 and P02-015 rather than as three spot fixes. Test the cure must pass: after the edit every cross-row reference in the row must resolve to a named verse that also appears in boundary_evidence_refs, and no sentence may name a rule, a part, or a position in place of evidence; note that the mirror arm was GREEN BEFORE the edit purely because the reference named no verse, so a GREEN re-run alone does not certify this cure - the reference must be read and resolved by hand.

The oath-site object re-counts to exactly four (MT 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 8:4) with הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ at oshb:Song.5.9 excluded on speech role - the daughters quoting the oath back - and the row both excludes and mirrors it. The parashah inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 8:4 under the claimed type and the row discloses it single-witness and corroborative. One qualification recorded rather than a defect: the row's 'fourth and last' universal sits in boundary_rationale while the digit that licenses it ('exactly four') sits in device_notes, so the digit is present in the row but not adjacent to that instance of the claim.
